declared.title: Positive fantasies about idealized futures sap energy
declared.foundIn: OpenAlex search « positive fantasies future motivation achievement » (2026-11-23)

population: 4 experiments with American undergraduates (n = 164, 50, 40, 80; Study 1 women only)

findings.text: Experimentally induced positive fantasies about a desired future left people less energized than questioning, negative or neutral fantasies

support.sentence: Induced positive fantasies resulted in less energy than fantasies that questioned the desired future (Study 1), negative fantasies (Study 2), or neutral fantasies (Study 3).
support.readBy: choose-your-struggle agent, 2026-11-23: abstract of the LSE accepted manuscript (eprints.lse.ac.uk/46284)

findings.text: In Study 3 (40 students), positive fantasies about the coming week went with lower self-reported accomplishment one week later

support.sentence: Indeed, accomplishment as reported a week later was lower in the positive fantasy than in the control condition, t(38)=2.00, p=.05, η2=.10 (Mpos=5.74, SD=1.36 versus Mcon=6.57, SD=1.26).
support.readBy: choose-your-struggle agent, 2026-11-23: LSE accepted manuscript (eprints.lse.ac.uk/46284), Study 3, Results

limits: small samples of American undergraduates; energy measured right after the induction (blood pressure, self-report)
achievement measured once, self-reported after one week, in a single study of 40 (p = .05)
one laboratory; no independent replication found
no abstract in Europe PMC, Crossref or OpenAlex: read in the authors' accepted manuscript
no sample from the Middle East or North Africa
allegiance: Oettingen developed fantasy realization theory and mental contrasting (WOOP), which she also promotes
